sections.title: Bangkok
sections.meta: 15–20 Oct · 5 nights · together · arriving from Hanoi
sections.intro: A working week with sightseeing bolted onto the afternoons, not a holiday. The base does more work than the itinerary here: everything below assumes a short walk to Asok and a room Os can take calls in at three in the morning without waking Jabari.

legend: Sun and Mon here are the SF weekend, so both are free

blocks.caption: Wat Arun from the Chao Phraya · photo miketnorton, CC BY 2.0

paragraphs: The hotel is booked, a short walk from Asok, where the BTS and the MRT cross. That puts the day trips, the river and the evenings all one change of train away.

The US weekend lands here as Sunday and Monday, so those two days are wide open and Saturday and Sunday nights have no 02:00 alarm behind them. Everything below is an option rather than a plan. Whatever appeals, and none of it if nothing does.

items.head: Evening only
items.text: Landing from Hanoi, so nothing planned.
Work night after. Home at a reasonable hour.

items.head: 13:00 → late
items.text: No calls that night, so the late one.

items.head: Full day → late
items.text: The best day of the week.

items.head: Full day → 21:30
items.text: Calls resume at 02:00 Tuesday.

items.head: Morning only
items.text: Jabari flies out, Os flies north.

paragraphs: **Arriving:** Hanoi to Suvarnabhumi is about 1h50. Grab to Sukhumvit runs 45–60 minutes and roughly 450 THB, or the Airport Rail Link if traffic is bad, changing at Phaya Thai. A SIM or an eSIM is easiest sorted at the airport.
Mid-October is the tail of the rainy season. Storms are heavy, usually mid-afternoon, and usually over within the hour. One indoor option in our pocket every day beats planning around the rain.

blocks.title: Afternoons
blocks.sub: Fits a 13:00 start on any day

items.title: Grand Palace & Wat Pho
items.text: The one thing a first-time visitor should not skip. Gold, mirrored glass, and the Emerald Buddha, then the enormous reclining Buddha next door. Hard deadline: the palace stops selling tickets at 15:30, so this only works if we leave on time. Covered shoulders and knees, enforced at the gate.

items.title: Wat Arun and the river
items.meta: 2 hours · 5 THB ferry from Tha Tien · best 17:00–19:00
items.text: Across the Chao Phraya, a climb up the porcelain-studded prang, then the view of it lit up from the Thonburi bank. Pairs naturally onto the end of a palace afternoon. The express boats home beat a taxi.

items.title: Chatuchak weekend market
items.meta: 3–4 hours · MRT Kamphaeng Phet · Sat & Sun to about 18:00
items.text: Fifteen thousand stalls, roughly a square kilometre of them. Two sections is plenty; the rest can be abandoned. Kamphaeng Phet puts us in the middle rather than at the edge, which matters more than it sounds.

items.title: Thonburi canals by longtail
items.meta: 2 hours · from Tha Chang or Tha Tien · about 1,500 THB per boat
items.text: The old city on the water side: stilt houses, temple landings, monitor lizards, and the Artist's House at Khlong Bang Luang. A whole boat to ourselves beats a tour, and late afternoon is when the light drops.

items.title: Chinatown by daylight
items.text: Different city from the night version. Wat Traimit holds five and a half tonnes of solid gold Buddha, and Talat Noi behind it is old shophouses, car-part workshops and street art. Ends where the food stalls set up.

items.title: Thai cooking class
items.text: Market trip first, then four or five dishes we actually cook. The good ones cap the group at eight. Entirely indoors, which makes it the strongest rain plan on this list.

blocks.title: Full days
blocks.sub: Needs Sunday the 18th or Monday the 19th

items.title: Ayutthaya
items.meta: 8–10 hours · car 1h15, or train from Krung Thep Aphiwat
items.text: The capital the Burmese burned in 1767, left as brick towers and headless Buddhas across a river island. Wat Mahathat has the famous Buddha head grown into fig roots. Bicycles are for hire at the site. Early is better: it is flat, shadeless and hot by eleven, and the towers stay floodlit until about 21:00 if we would rather go late instead.

items.title: Amphawa and the fireflies
items.meta: Afternoon and evening · Fri–Sun only · 1h30 each way
items.text: Out at 14:00, a stop at the Maeklong railway market where the awnings fold away as the train passes through, the canal market by 16:00, grilled river prawns off the boats, then a longtail out at dusk to trees full of synchronised fireflies. Back around 22:30, so it needs a free night.

items.title: Kanchanaburi
items.text: The bridge on the River Kwai, the Death Railway cut through cliffs above the water, the Allied war cemetery, and Erawan Falls with seven turquoise pools to swim in. Heavy history and a genuinely long day, but the most substantial thing within reach of Bangkok.

items.title: Bang Krachao by bike
items.meta: 4–5 hours · longtail across from Klong Toey pier
items.text: A jungle-covered oxbow in the river, six minutes from the city, laced with raised concrete paths through mangrove and palm. Bikes are for hire at the pier. The Bang Nam Pheung floating market runs weekends. Best in the morning before the heat.

items.title: Ancient City, Muang Boran
items.meta: 5–6 hours · BTS to Kheha then a short taxi
items.text: Two hundred hectares laid out in the shape of Thailand, holding full-scale reproductions of temples from every region. We cycle between them and there is almost nobody there. Strange, ambitious, and the opposite of a crowd.

items.title: Ko Kret
items.meta: 5 hours · taxi to Pak Kret, then a 5 THB ferry
items.text: A car-free island in the river north of the city, settled by Mon potters. The ring path is an hour on foot, with lunch and terracotta on the way. Liveliest on weekends, half-asleep midweek, which may be the point.

blocks.title: Evenings
blocks.sub: Any night, though Saturday and Sunday have no 02:00 alarm

items.title: Yaowarat street food
items.text: Bangkok's best eating happens on two blocks of Chinatown after dark. The queues worth joining are the ones the Thai families are in. The nine-day vegetarian festival may overlap our dates, since sources put it around 10–18 October: if it does, the street closes to traffic and turns into an enormous vegan food market instead.

items.title: Muay Thai at Rajadamnern
items.meta: From about 18:30 · MRT to Sam Yot then a short ride
items.text: The older of the two national stadiums, running since 1945. Live band, wild betting section, eight or nine bouts working up from teenagers to the main event. Ringside is worth it over the tourist tier.

items.title: Jodd Fairs night market
items.text: The current one, not the tourist-bus one. Food-first, packed with Thais, and ten minutes from the base by metro. Good default for a night when nothing is planned.

items.title: A rooftop
items.text: Octave at the Marriott Thonglor is three stops from the base and does not need a reservation. Vertigo at the Banyan Tree is higher and more formal. The riverside ones are the famous ones and priced accordingly.

items.title: Wat Pho massage school
items.text: The place the whole Thai massage tradition is taught from, attached to the temple. Proper deep work, not a spa. Cheap, and the correct response to a day that got rained out.

items.title: Jim Thompson House
items.meta: 90 minutes · BTS National Stadium · last tour late afternoon
items.text: Six teak houses assembled into one home by the American who rebuilt the Thai silk trade and then vanished in Malaysia in 1967. Short, shaded, air-conditioned in parts, and near the malls if the sky opens.

blocks.title: One way to arrange it
blocks.sub: If we would rather not decide

items.v: Jim Thompson House, then Wat Arun at sunset, then dinner on Yaowarat. Home by 22:00.
Chatuchak from 13:00, dinner in Thonglor, one rooftop. No alarm.
Grand Palace and Wat Pho at opening, car at 14:00 to Maeklong and Amphawa, fireflies after dark, back late.
Ayutthaya from 07:00, bicycles at the ruins, back by 18:30 for an early dinner before the calls.
Packing. Jabari flies out, Os flies to Chiang Mai.

paragraphs: The one real collision is Saturday. Chatuchak and Amphawa both want that afternoon and Amphawa only runs Friday to Sunday, so if we want both, Amphawa moves to Sunday and the palace moves to Sunday morning.

sections.text: 20 Oct · Don Mueang → Chiang Mai · Os heads north

sections.title: Chiang Mai
sections.intro: Late October is the good seam in the north: the rain has stopped, the burning season is months away, and the nights drop to something a person can sleep in. It is also the only week of this trip where the calls and the sightseeing do not fight each other, because most of what Os would do here happens in the morning or after dark.

items.title: Tamarind Village
items.text: Inside the walls, walking distance to Wat Chedi Luang and the Sunday market, quiet enough to work in. The obvious pick for five nights.

items.title: Rachamankha
items.text: Quieter and more austere, built like a Lanna temple compound. Fewer rooms, so it goes first.

items.title: 137 Pillars House
items.text: The comfortable option, teak colonial buildings and a long pool. Ten minutes from the old city by car, which is the trade.

items.title: Doi Suthep at first light
items.text: 06:00 is the time, before the coaches and while the monks are still chanting. The city sits under haze below the terrace. Straight back down for the calls if they shift, or make this a post-call trip on a day without sleep.

items.title: Doi Inthanon
items.text: The highest point in Thailand and the top of this trip's profile. Twin pagodas, the Ang Ka boardwalk through cloud forest, Wachirathan falls. A car and driver beats a minibus tour.

items.title: Elephant Nature Park
items.text: No riding, no bathing, no performances. It is the sanctuary the others copy the language of, and it sells out well in advance.

items.title: Both walking streets
items.text: Saturday is the silversmiths' road and the better of the two. Sunday runs through the old city and now falls inside the stay rather than on the day of the flight south. Both start around 16:00.

paragraphs: Two dates to know: 23 October is Chulalongkorn Day, a public holiday, so expect domestic crowds at Doi Suthep and Inthanon. 26 October is Ok Phansa, the end of Buddhist Lent, with dawn merit-making at the temples on the morning of the flight south.

blocks.caption: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep · photo Philip Nalangan, CC BY 4.0

sections.title: Khao Lak, by day trip
sections.meta: 26–31 Oct · two days on the water · solo
sections.intro: No liveaboard. The Similans sit 70 km offshore with no cell coverage, and a boat that keeps Os at sea for four nights during a working week is the one part of this trip that cannot bend. Day trips out of Khao Lak reach the same water, put Os back on a wifi connection every evening, and cost two days instead of five.

blocks.alt: The bay at Similan island number eight seen from the Sail Rock viewpoint
blocks.caption: Similan island 8 from Sail Rock · photo Mathias Krumbholz, CC BY-SA 3.0

items.title: Getting there, 26 Oct
items.sub: Chiang Mai → Khao Lak in one day
items.text: Flight CNX → Phuket, about 2h05 direct. Taxi north to Khao Lak, 1h15. Every day-trip operator wants divers in the shop the afternoon before to sign paperwork and try kit on, so land early enough to do that on the 26th.

items.title: The certification question
items.text: Thirty is the number the stricter operators ask for on Koh Tachai and Richelieu, so nothing is closed off. The logbook is worth bringing, since the dives that got there are recent enough that shops will want to see them.

blocks.title: Why not the boat
blocks.text: Four nights at sea means no connection, four dives a day, and calls landing at 02:00 with three hours of sleep either side. A handful of newer boats advertise wifi, which in practice is a satellite link nobody should plan a work week around. A Similan liveaboard done properly wants February to April and a week where diving is the point.

blocks.eyebrow: One day is enough, two if it goes well

items.note: The one that justifies the flight south. A single horseshoe pinnacle in open water, purple soft coral over every surface, macro on the walls and schooling fish above. Two dives on the same rock, and it does not get old. Long day: pickup around 06:30, back near 18:00.
The manta option. Limestone ridge at Koh Bon, then a current-swept pinnacle at Tachai with big schools. The better pick over the Similan boulder sites if there is only one more day.
Half day from Khao Lak, an old tin dredger broken into sections and covered in life. The only trip short enough to fit a normal working day, so hold it in reserve for a morning that goes wrong.

paragraphs: Depths are typical maximums, not a plan. Day trips are two dives each and leave at the posted time whether anyone is on it or not. Richelieu is the one to book first, and the second day can wait until after seeing how the 02:00 calls and a 06:30 pickup feel stacked together.

items.title: If the second day is too much
items.text: The 29th becomes a working day and the flight out is a rested one. Nothing else in the plan moves, and the no-fly buffer only gets longer.

items.title: If Richelieu gets cancelled
items.text: Weather cancels the far northern trips first, since it is the longest crossing. Ask the shop to roll the booking to the next running day, and keep the local wrecks as the version that sails when the outer trips do not.

blocks.caption: Richelieu Rock · photo Mr.CMBurns, CC BY-SA 4.0

items.title: Khao Lak Explorer
items.text: One of the few shops already running in late October, and they do Richelieu as a day trip. Speedboat out to a larger dive platform, so the crossing is fast and the day is not.

items.title: Sea Dragon
items.text: The other Khao Lak shop worth an email, and the one with wrecks and house reefs on the menu for a short morning. Free dive computer on Similan trips.

items.title: Big Blue Diving
items.text: Their site says day trips restart in November, so confirm the exact restart date before building the week around them. Worth asking because they run Richelieu more often than anyone.

items.title: 28 Oct · the working day
items.text: Deliberately empty. Calls at 02:00, sleep, then a desk and a pool. Two diving days in a row on this sleep schedule is how the second one gets done badly.

items.title: 30 Oct · no-fly day
items.text: Twenty-four hours between the last dive and the first flight. Last dive is the morning of the 29th, so this is covered twice over. Beach, massage, the Police Boat 813 memorial inland.

items.title: 31 Oct → 1 Nov
items.text: Taxi to Phuket 1h15, HKT → BKK 1h25, one night near Suvarnabhumi. Bangkok to Manila is 3h20 direct the next day.

blocks.caption: Khao Lak · photo Vyacheslav Argenberg, CC BY 4.0

sections.title: The order to book in
sections.meta: The first two set every other date

items.lead: Two day trips out of Khao Lak.
items.text: Richelieu on the 27th, Koh Bon and Tachai on the 29th. Worth confirming the shop is running that week before booking flights south, since several restart in November.
The hotel near Asok is booked.
DMK → CNX on the 20th, CNX → HKT on the 26th, HKT → BKK on the 31st, BKK → MNL on the 1st.

items.lead: Chiang Mai, six nights, and Elephant Nature Park.
items.text: The sanctuary books out further ahead than the hotels do.
DAN or equivalent with hyperbaric cover. Shops ask for proof at check-in and will sell a daily policy to anyone who turns up without one.
Full afternoon and evening, booked through the hotel or a private driver.
Free, mandatory, and only accepted within 72 hours of arrival, so it cannot be done early.

items.title: Entry
items.text: Both our passports enter without a visa. The permitted stay has been 60 days and is in the middle of being cut back toward 30; either covers 17 days. Six months of passport validity and the onward Manila ticket as proof of exit.

items.title: TDAC
items.text: The digital arrival card replaced the paper form and is now required of every foreign national. It is free and the only real portal is tdac.immigration.go.th. Everything charging for it is a scam.

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Grab for cars, Bolt as the cheaper backup, never a flagged street taxi in Bangkok. The MRT takes contactless cards directly; the BTS is smoother with a Rabbit card from any station booth.

items.title: Money
items.text: Cards work in malls and restaurants, cash everywhere else. ATMs charge a flat 220 THB per withdrawal regardless of amount, so pull large sums rarely.

items.title: Weather
items.text: Mid-October Bangkok is the tail of the wet season: hot, humid, with hard afternoon storms that pass in an hour. Chiang Mai is drier and cool at night. The Andaman is still settling, so expect swell on the 70 km crossing and visibility below the February peak.

items.title: Diving and flying
items.text: Twenty-four hours between the last dive and the first flight is the floor. Last dive is the morning of the 29th and the first flight is the 31st, which leaves two clear days and absorbs a boat that comes back late.
